I think, like folks have been saying, that there are multiple factors in play. Like shimage said, the most objective evidence we have available says that Expat, Fixer, Bunker, and AZ consistently lose more than other heroes. I think we can agree that, with those 4 heroes especially, when you get an off hand, it really hurts the team. To go to the complete opposite end of the spectrum, with Dark Visionary, if you played no cards but spied the villain deck every turn, she'd probably still have an above-average win rate (and I'll go ahead and disagree pretty vehemently that DV is less interactive than Expat, though we can save that debate for another thread :-p). With Wraith's stats jumping like they did, I think you can look at her deck and say, "Wow, those low stats are really an anomaly, and it makes sense that she trended toward the average." Now, personal opinion, I still think 75% is low for Wraith, but I just happen to think she's one of the 3 or 4 best heroes in the game for any team :)

Another factor is enjoyment, and people are trying to anchor enjoyment objectively, but that's really hard to do. For instance, of the four heroes above, I love playing Fixer, I enjoy AZ and Bunker, and I'm trying to play more Expat to get a more educated opinion about her. I could list off a dozen reasons why I love Fixer (and I probably have in another thread or two), but I also understand that he has a weakness, and that weakness can really kill his games (see: 68% win rate). Though don't be shocked if Fixer's win rate pulls a Wraith, because I think that, early on, people tried to play him as a damage dealer, when he's definitely not (he can fill very specific niches when he needs to, but he's not in any real damage dealer's league).

I have another anecdotal "Expat hater" reason why I find her frustrating: I had just about as ideal as a starting hand as possible (Shotgun, Quick Draw, Arsenal Access, and the Assault Rifle, the environment let me play a second quick draw on like the third turn) against advanced Ennead (with Bunker, Ra, and Scholar). Very long story short, Ra also had the perfect start (imbued fire, solar flare x2, fire immunity), and he got 2 or 3 staves out for the heals, so by the time I got to 8 damage in one turn (P&P, imbued fire, hollow points), I was dead, but Ra was still in good shape. So when I died, I just startged supplying Ra or Bunker with an extra power (9 damage to one or 4-4-3), instantly outstripping the output I could have done on my own save for very specific setup (SMG/Imbued Fire/Hollow Points or Unload). I totally understand and agree that it's unfair to use the perfect Ra setup as the example of Expat contributing more dead than alive, but I was primed to just dominate, but instead I got nickel & dimed to death, dealt a fair amount of damage, and then dealt more damage by allowing someone else to use a power. It was both the best and worst scenario for playing Expat. The most frustrating thing was I had to discard a card early on, so that meant that the entire rest of the game, I had a hand of 3, because I had no means of getting extra cards outside of Scholar's one shots.

My favorite homemade Expat base power is this one: destroy a gun to draw 3 cards (2 if you think that's too powerful?). If the only weapon in your initial draw is SMG and you're fighting Iron Legacy, you can get 1-2 skipped turns' worth of cards and hopefully get something on the table and pumping out damage the next turn instead of 2-3 turns later.

posts.name: Octavian
posts.cooked:
To be clear, I'm proposing this as alt power for a Promo Hero version of Fixer - not as a "fix" to the character.   I think he works fine as is, but I spent some time the other night brainstorming how an alternate hero card would work considering his reliance on Strike.  Yes, it's a major change, but making a new power named Strike that also does damage isn't interesting and I enjoyed the puzzle of coming up with an alternate power that still lets him function. 

 

I dubbed it "Anticipate" because you are setting up your next turn most of the time, but thematically and mechanically it might be better named "Focus" because (mechancially) it really narrows how Fixer gets played and (thematically) it fits with the Martial Artist theme of digging into his wealth of fighting knowledge to take the perfect approach for the situation.  He can always get out the style he wants.  He can always get out Harmony.  The only question mark is if he has the best tool for the job. 

Yes, it makes some cards useless.  But not totally useless as they are easy options for the Discard part of the power.

Yes, deck searching can take a bit of time.  But it won't take that much becuase once this Fixer is at the point where he's using Charge every turn it is right on the top of the Discard to nab.

Maybe he won't be as much fun to play, but some people already have that criticism of Fixer.  And I know plenty of people who would enjoy getting out the perfect Style for the situation and hammering it.  Eventually Fixer will have a Grease Gun in his hand or a better tool and there will be the tension of when to use it vs wait and Charge again.

I think I put this in another thread, but my idea for a promo Fixer's base power is: "Take a Swipe - Fixer deals 1 target 0 damage. Draw a card." Of course, when he gets other cards in play that increase his damage, this power starts actually dealing damage, but IMO this would get more tools and styles into his hand, giving him more flexibility to swap them out as necessary. It'd be like always playing with TLT, except losing his early damage (and let's face it, if you're using Fixer as a primary damage hero outside of a couple specific niches, you're doing it wrong :-p ).

I actually got the idea from this Expat thread, as someone suggested a 0-damage base power to let her use her ammo. I'm not personally a fan of that for Expat, but I like the idea for Fixer. I'll try it sometime and report how it goes.

Edit: this also gives Fixer cause to use his double-power one-shot early in the game; I'm always gun-shy with using it before either A) I've got Harmony and a good damage tool out or B) I really need an extra point or two of damage to put a target down.
